newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac confirms BML merger approved.
newsitem.headline: Westpac confirms BML merger approved.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp and Bank of Melbourne Ltd said on Friday they had received approval from the Reserve Bank of Australia and Australia's anti-competition watchdog, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), for their proposed merger.
Bank of Melbourne executive chairman Christopher Stewart said he was pleased Australian Treasurer Peter Costello, the RBA and the ACCC had approved the merger.
Stewart said the approvals cleared the way to create a stronger and more vigorous competitor in the banking market in Victoria state.

The two banks had given the ACCC a range of undertakings, including that the autonomy of Bank of Melbourne management would be retained and that normal opening hours and local debit card operations would be kept.
Fee-free banking would also be kept for Bank of Melbourne customers who maintain personal account balances of over A$400.
Other undertakings were also given regarding access to Westpac's ATM/EFTPOS network.
"The undertakings given by both Bank of Melbourne and Westpac are consistent with the proposed approach to this merger," Stewart said in a statement.

"Bank of Melbourne will be combined with the Victorian retail and commercial operations of Westpac and the merged business will be carried on as Bank of Melbourne with strong local management," he said.
Stewart said the bank's board believed the merger was in the best interests of shareholders, customers and staff.
"Our identity, our strong customer relationships and our high standards of cost-effective service will be adopted throughout the combined branch network," he said.
"The merger with Westpac will create a new competitive force in Victoria and offer our customers a much broader range of products and financial services," he said.
Merger details will be sent to shareholders and a meeting to vote on the proposal will be called for late September.
Westpac executive director John Morschel welcomed the merger approval and said customers of both banks would benefit from it.
"The Bank of Melbourne name will be retained and its customers can be confident the merger will bring about a stronger regional bank within a national network," Merschel said in a statement.
"This will ensure Bank of Melbourne remains a vigorous and effective competitor in Victoria," he said.
"Bank of Melbourne brings to the merger its outstanding customer service and regional focus while Westpac will deliver its award winning product range," he said.
By 12.35 p.m. (0235 GMT), Westpac shares were up eights cents at A$8.21 on trade of 11.6 million shares.
However the bulk of the transactions were in pre-opening trade on the exercise of July series options which expired on Thursday.
Bank of Melbourne shares were up 14.2 cents to A$9.80, with 2.2 million shares traded.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
